images.title: Three ways to show data
images.purpose: Show that the same data can be shown as a table, a pictograph or a bar graph, and the picture forms make comparing easy.
images.composition: Three small panels in one row with wide space between them and a title word under each.
images.exact_structure: Same data in all three: Apples 4, Bananas 2. Panel 1: a table with 2 rows (Apples 4, Bananas 2). Panel 2: a pictograph, apples row of exactly 4 teal #0072B2 circles, bananas row of exactly 2 amber #E69F00 circles. Panel 3: a bar graph with a teal bar exactly 4 units tall and an amber bar exactly 2 units tall, equal widths. Same size panels. Exactly 3 panels.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
different numbers in the three panels, or panels of different sizes
images.takeaway: The same data can be shown three ways; pictures make comparing quicker.
images.description: Three equal panels showing Apples 4 and Bananas 2 as a table, a pictograph of 4 and 2 circles, and a bar graph with bars 4 and 2 units tall.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to find the bigger number in each panel and say which form shows it fastest.

image_decisions.why: The choice of display is the single idea; one data set across three panels keeps it clear.
